title: An empty flattened map: reconstructToMap returns a partial map, reconstruct() disagrees
rationale: The missing/empty-input drill doctrine requires of every new gate, and a real asymmetry rather than a ceremonial one. reconstructToMap early-returns createEmptyRecord for an empty flattened map, which populates only defaulted and nullable fields. reconstruct() then feeds that partial map to mapToGenericRecord, whose GenericRecordBuilder.build() has to answer for a required field with no default. Two sibling methods give the same input two different answers about whether it is representable - the same shape as avro-flattened-name-collision-guard-fires.
catchesBugClass: A degenerate-input path that diverges between two public entry points, and a builder that reports a missing required field only on one of them. Also catches the empty-map early return being deleted or widened.
cannotCatch: It cannot tell you which of the two answers is CORRECT - arguably both throwing, or both returning a partial map, would be defensible; it only pins that they disagree. It also does not cover a partially-populated flattened map, which is the far more common Spark case and reaches a different branch.

predicted.detail: UNCERTAIN AND FLAGGED: depends on what MapFlattener.flatten({}) returns. If it returns an empty map, reconstructToMap early-returns {region:null} and reconstruct() throws on the required id. The recorder decides; if measurement contradicts DEFECT the manifest publishes the measurement and an override records the disagreement.

expected.avroDoc: THROWN: AvroMissingFieldException: Field id type:STRING pos:0 not set and has no default value
